A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same work. Their equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching the retained experiments and generation examples.

before.justification: v1 reports original LM1B and OpenWebText experiments, including generation metrics in Table 1, training curves in Figures 1–3 and generated examples in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds training-cost measurements, sampling-step comparisons, zero-shot evaluations and 1.1B-model results, including classifier-free guidance experiments.

M1.justification: The central denoising and negative-sampling objectives are retained; the anti-uniform KL formulation reinterprets the existing SDDLM-V1 loss. v2 adds an auxiliary unsupervised classifier-free guidance procedure that rescales prompt-conditioned predictions against random-token-conditioned predictions for likelihood and generation (Section 4.4). It also introduces a larger model configuration using RMSNorm and SwiGLU.

E1.justification: v2 retains LM1B/OWT and adds SlimPajama pretraining; zero-shot perplexity evaluation on WikiText, LAMBADA, AG News, PubMed and ArXiv; and downstream evaluation on ARC-e, BoolQ, HellaSwag, OpenBookQA, PIQA, RACE and SIQA, plus LAMBADA next-word prediction. This substantially expands the represented domains and task requirements.

E2.justification: v1's reported comparisons use Duo. v2 Table 3 additionally compares against SEDD-Uniform, UDLM and PLAID, using their cited results, while Figure 3 includes an AR reference. Table 7 also compares guided variants, substantially broadening the comparison methods.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce 1.1B models, Llama-2 tokenization, 2,048-token contexts and batch size 256, alongside zero-shot likelihood and downstream evaluation protocols. Figures 2–3 add a matched-batch, 0.5-epoch cost comparison and an 8–1,024-step sampling sweep. The original 170M, one-million-step training setup remains.

E4.justification: v2 adds sampling-step sensitivity analysis (Figure 3), direct training-time and memory comparisons (Figure 2), and CFG-on/off and cross-method guidance analyses (Tables 1 and 7). These investigate efficiency and guidance beyond v1's loss comparisons. The four appendix generation examples are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, standard deviations or statistical significance tests. The additional experiments retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: v1 Table 1 is preserved numerically as v2 Table 2, and the appendix samples are unchanged. v2 adds substantial results for efficiency, sampling budgets, zero-shot perplexity and downstream tasks. For example, Table 4 reports LAMBADA scores of 17.02, 26.53 and 31.75 for Duo, SDDLM and SDDLM-V1. These are newly reported evaluations, not improvements over matching v1 runs.

T1.justification: v2 adds a short derivation connecting uniform-to-model KL divergence with the retained random-negative objective (Section 4.2 and Appendix A.1), plus an explicit attractive/repulsive gradient expression (Equation 10). This adds limited mathematical reasoning without new theorems or convergence guarantees.

C1.justification: v1 leaves larger models and more complex tasks to future work; v2 claims demonstrated effectiveness up to 1.1B parameters and uses this to support large-scale pretraining. It also elevates mitigation of uniform-output degeneration to an explicit contribution, while retaining the original loss-simplification and generation-quality claims.

C2.justification: v2 develops a new mechanism explanation: negative gradients counter overly uniform predictions under heavy corruption, with an attractive/repulsive interpretation in Sections 4.2–4.3. It expands the likelihood-versus-generation discussion to ELBO bounds and downstream performance. Conversely, v1's discussion of direct NCE instability and sensitivity to negative-sample counts is removed.

D1.justification: v2 adds large-model architecture, tokenizer, optimizer and 16-H800 hardware details; zero-shot preprocessing instructions; CFG weight 1.1; and training/evaluation descriptions with pseudocode in Appendices B–C. Curriculum training is documented more explicitly without establishing a change to the original procedure. The small-model hyperparameters and repository link are retained.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning beyond the earlier diffusion-language-model discussion, adding denoising autoencoders, contrastive learning, representation alignment, CFG and recent USDM scaling research. Examples include Vincent et al., Chen et al. (2020), Xiang et al., Yu et al., Ho and Salimans, and von Rütte et al.; these additions support new conceptual connections.

P1.justification: The abstract and conclusion are substantially rewritten, the introduction gains an explicit contribution summary, and the former unified method discussion becomes four named subsections. Related work is subdivided, and the appendices are reorganized into derivations, hyperparameters, experimental details and retained generation examples.

P2.justification: v2 switches the main text and references from one to two columns, resizes and relocates retained figures and tables, and reformats the sample boxes. It adds cost and sampling-step figures, downstream and guidance tables, a large-model hyperparameter table and an algorithm block. These are substantial visual changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v1 demonstrates generation quality only for small models and leaves efficiency largely unmeasured and larger-scale applicability untested. v2 adds direct resource measurements, sampling-budget analysis, broader comparisons and 1.1B downstream evaluations, substantially strengthening the evidence for practical usefulness. Added implementation details also help assessment. Large-model training budgets and statistical uncertainty remain insufficiently documented, and the proposed uniform-collapse mechanism lacks a targeted ablation, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial empirical gains.
